Job metadata is verbatim from the stored artifact record (list_artifacts_by_request via the platform bridge, 2026-09-03). The `data` object is RECONSTRUCTED from the rendered PDF's observed defects and from the bridge's brand-injection code path (pdf-render-brand.ts / mcp-tool-handlers.ts) — the live payload lives in the pdf-render-data store under renderDataRef and is not readable over MCP. It reproduces all three defect classes exactly: (1) `brand` arrives as an object where the template slots it as a string -> `[object Object]` twice, (2) p2Body..p5Body absent -> four blank content pages under non-strict Liquid, (3) image slots hold site-relative /img/ paths that render-service cannot resolve -> aborted requests and broken-image boxes.

expectedDefects._blankContentPagesNote: Page 5 is NOT caught by a text-length rule: it renders 56 characters, all of them the [object Object] token plus the boilerplate disclaimer. It is caught by the UNRENDERED_TOKEN rule instead. This is exactly why the quality gate needs both rules and why a page-count/bytes check (inspect.ts today) sees nothing wrong.
